title: Weather Station
strapline: Watching the sky — noticing, recording and talking about the weather.
intent: Watching and recording the weather helps children notice change and the passing of time.
The weather connects children to the seasons and to caring for themselves (coats, sun cream).
Simple recording brings early data-handling and counting into a real context.
Weather is a rich source of "why" and "what will happen" questions.
Rich weather vocabulary grows through daily, purposeful talk.
implementation: Set up a daily weather-watch: look out or step outside and talk about what you see and feel.
Record the weather on a simple chart with symbols the children choose and place.
Link the weather to what we do and wear — "it's raining, what will we need?".
Add real tools: a rain gauge, a windsock, a thermometer to read together.
Count and compare over the week — "how many rainy days so far?".
Follow children's wonderings about clouds, puddles, wind and frost.
key_questions: What is the weather doing today?
What will we need to wear or take outside?
How many sunny days have we had this week?
Where do you think the puddle went?
Why do you think it is windy today?

impact.text: Children notice weather and seasons and what they mean for us.
Children ask questions about the weather and offer their own ideas.
Children record and compare the weather, counting days over time.
Children use rich vocabulary to describe what they see and feel outdoors.
Children link the weather to caring for their own bodies and needs.

enhancements: A weather chart with child-made symbols and a pointer.
A rain gauge, windsock and simple thermometer.
Weather-appropriate clothing so all weathers can be experienced.
Magnifiers and containers for investigating puddles, frost and ice.
Books and songs about weather and the seasons.
A window view or easy outdoor access for daily watching.

playing_exploring: Children observe the changing weather closely and with curiosity.
active_learning: Children keep up the daily watch and notice patterns over the week.
creating_thinking: Children ask why and predict what the weather might do next.
